Lessons.Title: Measure in Halves and Fourths of an Inch
ExplanationParagraphs: Original 2021 Grade 3 Unit6 Lesson3 aligns CCSS 3.MD.B.4 and 3.NF.A.3.c. Local teacher HTML and preparation files are inspected individually on Our-CS: lesson.html SHA256 393836f406f6bcb5e28e71e88502e76fa66d976e09ea5ccb940550c3c48718bc; preparation.html SHA256 bb6995a6c3904628fea51b4dca6bf471e2ce259f4e9c3fa70e15a034c2e73945. Public original student-facing HTML sections are indexed and manually compared; a separate original Student Task Statements PDF, physical ruler blackline-master and source worm illustration pixels remain unreviewed.

Warm-up Notice and Wonder: Rulers (10 minutes): compare the TWO earlier pupil-made rulers (halves and fourths separately) with a newly supplied ruler marked with BOTH half-inch and quarter-inch ticks. The NEW ruler has visually distinguished whole, half, and quarter tick types. Teacher blackline ruler is handed to EACH pupil; pairs discuss observations. The original teacher highlights that some rulers have zero on the left physical edge while others have a margin: always check WHERE the zero tick actually sits. Multiple student observations are valid; no numeric answer key.

Activity1 Halves and Quarters (15 minutes), first question: the original worm on a combined half/quarter inch ruler has one length labelled by Kiran as 4 2/4 inches and by Jada as 4 1/2 inches. BOTH are mathematically correct because 2/4=1/2 measured in the SAME one-inch unit, so the length is 4 1/2 inches or 18/4 inches. The exercise tests equivalent representations and explanations, not competing correct/incorrect pupil claims.

Activity1 then has FOUR distinct ORIGINAL worm illustrations A,B,C,D that pupils must measure using the same ruler with both kinds of marks. Original PUBLIC teacher synthesis explicitly identifies worm A as 4 inches, equivalently 8/2 or16/4; worm D as 3 1/2 inches, equivalently3 2/4,7/2 or14/4. Those ARE verified source teacher statements. Worms B and C have no fixed textual measurements in the local source extract; their original illustration pixels were not inspected. Do NOT invent B or C scalar values; teacher must measure/read the actual original figures, verify alignment and accept other equivalent fraction names.

The source teacher asks why a worm may be measured correctly when its LEFT endpoint is not aligned with zero on the pictured ruler: subtract the location of one endpoint from the location of the other rather than reading the right endpoint alone. An object's length is right-position minus left-position in inches if both are on the same ruler scale. If a student uses the physical ruler edge instead of the ruler's zero or doesn't subtract two nonzero endpoints, teacher checks that error.

Activity2 Measure and Describe (25 minutes) has TWO original student directions. First, EACH group chooses AT LEAST ONE classroom object whose measured length is a WHOLE number of inches and AT LEAST THREE objects whose measured lengths are NOT whole inches, for AT LEAST FOUR actual classroom objects in the original object/length table. They use the combined half/quarter ruler; no exact room-object numbers can be preset in a textbook key. Second, TRADE the measured-object lists with ANOTHER group, find a reported length that can be rewritten in an equivalent form, and record original object, original length and equivalent length in the second original table. The number of valid rewrites depends on students' measurements.

Original source synthesis: 5 1/2 inches=5 2/4 inches, and 1 1/4 inches=5/4 inches but cannot be exactly expressed as a multiple of 1/2 inch. Source also suggests 7 whole inches=14/2 inches=28/4 inches; distinguish using half-inch/quarter-inch mark while preserving SAME whole unit. MLR8 discussion supports partner practice in speaking about equivalent fractions. The source teacher-only Cool-down How Long? and physical blackline ruler artwork were not accessed; copyrighted worm images are not copied. .NET source tests authored only and not run; Stage D/CI, published app content and academic approval have not been verified.

KeyConcepts.Title: One combined ruler
KeyConcepts.Definition: A ruler with marks for whole inches, halves and fourths can name some positions in more than one equivalent way.
KeyConcepts.Rule: 1/2 inch=2/4 inch; length at k+1/2 also at k+2/4.

KeyConcepts.Title: One physical length, several fraction names
KeyConcepts.Definition: Equivalent fractions have the same point/distance even if numerator and denominator differ.
KeyConcepts.Rule: a/b=c/d when ad=bc and same unit is used.

KeyConcepts.Title: Measure between nonzero marks
KeyConcepts.Definition: Length of a segment is a difference between endpoint coordinates on the same linear inch ruler.

KeyConcepts.Title: Quarter not always a half-increment
KeyConcepts.Definition: A quantity with fractional remainder 1/4 or 3/4 cannot be named as a whole multiple of a half inch.
KeyConcepts.Example: Measure using the quarter-inch ticks to capture one quarter exactly.

WorkedExamples.Title: Kiran and Jada original worm
WorkedExamples.Question: Kiran says4 2/4 inches; Jada says4 1/2 inches. Who is correct?
WorkedExamples.Method: Compare the fractional remainders on the same whole-inch unit.
Steps: Two fourths cover half a whole inch.
Their two mixed-number lengths are equal.

WorkedExamples.Title: Source worm A
WorkedExamples.Question: State three source-confirmed names for worm A's length.
WorkedExamples.Method: Identify whole four-inches and re-express as halves/fourths.
Steps: All names refer to same ruler length.
WorkedExamples.Check: Original teacher synthesis expressly verifies these.

WorkedExamples.Title: Source worm D
WorkedExamples.Question: State four source-confirmed length names for worm D.
WorkedExamples.Method: Convert3 1/2 into fourths and improper fractions.
WorkedExamples.Check: Source teacher synthesis explicitly lists all four.

WorkedExamples.Title: Physical endpoint alignment
WorkedExamples.Question: A worm starts at ruler location1 1/4 and ends at4 3/4 inches. How long is it?
WorkedExamples.Check: Independent teaching example, NOT an invented numeric length for source worms B/C.

WorkedExamples.Title: Classroom lengths and group trade
WorkedExamples.Question: Can another group rename an observed length 5 1/2 inches?
WorkedExamples.Method: Keep same actual object length and convert half to fourths.
Steps: Half an inch equals two fourths.
Record the observed object and both length labels.
WorkedExamples.Check: Whether any real object has that length depends on students' measurement.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Mark Kiran wrong and Jada right despite both measuring same worm.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Show ruler position and fraction equivalence.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Invent precise worm B or C lengths from alt-text only.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: These source figures have not been visually measured on device.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Leave teacher-source diagram comparison open for those two.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Assume ruler's physical left edge is always zero.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: Source explicitly contrasts rulers with a zero margin versus edge zero.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Check zero position and subtract physical endpoints when starting above zero.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Declare 1 1/4 is exactly a number of half-inch steps.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: 1 1/4 is halfway between 1 and1 1/2, requiring quarter-inch precision.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Substitute one student-generated item for the original four physical object classes.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: Source specifies at least one whole-length object and at least three non-whole-length objects.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Keep four observed objects and complete traded-list equivalence task.

SummaryPoints: Original lesson combines whole/half/quarter marks on one ruler; students compare it with two old rulers and must check actual zero location.
Source Kiran 4 2/4 and Jada 4 1/2 are BOTH correct for same original worm.
Four source worm drawings A–D: teacher text verifies A=4=8/2=16/4, D=3 1/2=3 2/4=7/2=14/4; B/C remains figure-review task, not guessed.
Activity2 asks at least ONE whole-number and THREE non-whole lengths from classroom objects, followed by trading lists between groups and rewriting equivalents.
Publisher original standalone pupil PDF, worm/ruler art and restricted Cool-down unverified; tests/Stage D unexecuted.
